title: PDEs Seminar – Miles Wheeler (University of Bath)
desc:
Title. Overdetermined problems for the Helmholtz equation

Abstract. We consider overdetermined problems for the Helmholtz equation where one asks for both constant Dirichlet data and constant Neumann data on the entire boundary. It is easy to find explicit radial solutions when the domain is a ball. For zero Neumann data, there is a famous conjecture, attributed to Schiffer, that balls are the only solutions. For zero Dirichlet data, there is a less famous conjecture, attributed to Berenstein, that balls are the only solutions. When both the Dirichlet data and Neumann data can be nonzero, there is an even less famous conjecture, made first by Willms–Gladwell and then by Williams, that balls are the only solutions.

title: Junior Dynamics Seminar – Ross Ah-Weng
desc:
Statistical Degradation of Chaotic Dynamical Systems on Computers

Speaker: Ross Ah-Weng

Abstract : Many chaotic physical systems are forecasted using Birkhoff averages of observables along numerically simulated trajectories. However, when any dynamical system is simulated in floating-point arithmetic, the continuum is replaced by a finite discrete domain. The new dynamics are substantially different: every trajectory is eventually periodic, sufficiently close trajectories become indistinguishable after roundoff, and any invariant measure is supported on a finite set of disjoint periodic orbits. We identify a generic mechanism in which non-injectivity from rounding causes statistics inferred from any simulated trajectory to continually and irreversibly degrade. We develop this framework…

title: SIAM Junior Applied Mathematics Seminar (JAMS) – Pablo Zurita Soler & Kamaljit Singh
desc:
Modelling active fluid-structure interaction in the microscale through Lagrangian mechanics

Speaker : Pablo Zurita Soler

Abstract: When observing biological fluids, it is common to find flows that arise as a direct result of the motion of solids in contact with them. Biological and biomedical solids are said to be active when they themselves generate their own motion, typically by creating stress via internal mechanisms. Modelling such mechanisms presents a number of challenges, even more so when considering the hydrodynamic coupling present via the fluid-structure interaction.

title: GATP Seminar – Geordie Williamson (Sydney)
desc: Intersection (co)homology is a beautiful invariant of singular spaces, e.g. singular complex algebraic varieties. Over the rationals it satisfies a raft of strong properties (e.g. Poincaré duality, hard Lefschetz, pure Hodge structure,…) which still seem like a miracle. In their paper introducing these groups, Goresky and MacPherson point out that (unlike the integral cohomology of smooth manifolds) it fails to satisfy Poincaré duality over the integers. Subsequent sheaf theoretic approaches have clarified the situation, and in fact one can prove that there is no reasonable theory over the integers which satisfies Poincaré duality. I will discuss intersection cohomology, given several simple examples that illustrate the theory. Then I will discuss work in progress with F. Klein and T.…

title: SPC Seminar – Climate – Joshua Duffield (Imperial)
desc:
Title: Seasonal cycle of surface temperature: insights from simple models

Speaker: Joshua Duffield (Imperial)

Abstract: From the perspective of the annual harmonic, the role of surface heat capacity in controlling the seasonal cycle of surface temperature is readily apparent: a larger heat capacity leads to a greater lag (i.e., the time delay between peak incoming solar radiation and the hottest day of the year), as well as a reduced seasonal amplitude (i.e., the difference between summer and winter temperatures). Over the ocean, changes in heat capacity in response to global warming can therefore drive opposing amplitude trends.
